program: Donated surgical access: finite earlier-care portfolio

nutshell.headline: A selected colonoscopy price does not describe an ordinary Operation Access gift.
nutshell.body: Central whole-gift national donor $15,609,221 and gross-associated resources $57,020,662 per10 QALYs. Bay $26,015,369 / $95,034,437; SF $195,115,266 / $712,758,277. Local shares are weak priors.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: OA coordinates real donated specialist care for uninsured people, potentially accelerating needed procedures. First-eye cataract evidence supports finite health gains in a different clinical population.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: Most portfolio health remains unquantified; the credited subsets, alternative-care delays and donor-to-capacity effect are uncertain. The legacy selectedSF$600,000 is not this whole-gift estimate.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: Verify specialty cash allocation, unique symptomatic case mix, local residence, alternative-care timing and available donated provider capacity before recommending a gift.

programSection.body: Ambulatory Surgery Access Coalition dbaOperationAccess, EIN94-3180356, matches uninsured Northern California/Central Valley patients to donated specialist procedures. Current eligibility excludes people eligible for full-scopeMedi-Cal, Medicare orCMSP. OA is not comprehensive insurance. Official ordinary giving route verified without transaction.

steps.title: Whole portfolio
steps.detail: 2025:1,529services, including575GI,201general surgery and45ophthalmology; other gynecology, orthopedic, head/neck, urologic, skin and vascular care remains in the portfolio.

steps.title: Incremental unique clinical subsets
steps.detail: Budget allocation→service equivalents→additional provider capacity→selected condition→unique disjoint people. Service counts and94%appointment readiness are not health gains.

steps.title: Earlier care, not never care
steps.detail: Finite symptom relief or finite survival difference versus eventual ordinary care. Procedure harms remain separate.

programSection.boundary: All ten cash allocations sum to one. Other services retain full costs with health unquantified; zero credit is not a finding they are ineffective. This partial-health whole-gift estimate is not an upper bound on cost-effectiveness. Completed-service cost includes coordination, overhead and failed referrals. Selected clinical subset, service-to-person conversion, financial additionality and disjointness are separate assumptions; service count alone is never a health outcome. Current uninsured/ineligible-Medi-Cal eligibility is not a never-care baseline. Later safety-net care, coverage changes, other donors, donated provider capacity and OA's existing navigation remain in the counterfactual. CRC uses an explicitly judgmental mean-hazard survival approximation. Cohort mortality association and navigationRCT are not causal manufacturer-like coefficients; no .13 completion multiplier or legacy aggregate.05Q is reused. One exclusive linked-person ledger CRC then eye then hernia. Repeats/second eyes and overlapping diagnoses retain costs but cannot earn duplicate whole-person health. No productivity, caregiver or other mortality gains are added. Donated clinical resources, distinct nonclinical support, patient time and downstream cancer-care allowances are gross associated costs on all nominal services, including uncredited/replaced activity. They are not waived charges, net incremental resources, or exhaustive societal cost. Both health comparisons start with the same people alive at care. Delay discounts only; horizons start at care, not gift. Harms are already gift-date PV and include repeat procedures within an episode; late-comparator harms are not subtracted. Bay and SF are nested weak residence priors, not measured local return. US equals all-region direct health here; no international or indirect local spillovers are credited. Historical selectedSF$600,000 donor/$1,012,000 expanded price remains a separate program comparison. It must not remain the ordinary-gift ranking input after this revision.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: Cautious and signed cases can cause net harm. Unquantified services can improve true value, but may also carry unmeasured harms: this is not a proven cost upper bound. Favorable case was not tuned to a threshold.
model.fundingBoundary: 2025largest-funder loss, layoffs and other-donor growth coexist with16monthsoperatingcash. The2026$1.9Mbudget is a plan, not a measured capacity contraction or marginal offer. Donation restriction, local slots and financing leverage remain unverified.

comparisonBridge.headline: Historical selected abnormal-FIT comparison, preserved
comparisonBridge.body: Legacy conditionalSFmodel assumed$1,500 cash per completed pathway,50%additionality and.05aggregate netQALY. It did not allocate an ordinary whole gift to geography or other services. This revision replaces its ranking interpretation, not its archived arithmetic.
comparisonBridge.boundary: Do not blend the historical aggregate.05Q with the new finite hazard/symptom model or present either as measuredOAhealth. No new organization count.

evidence.design: Primary audited accounts and annual report
evidence.transfer: Counts inform composition only; specialty cash spending, selected diagnoses and unique-persons are unknown.
Differentage/sex/vision severity and counterfactual. .05utilitypoint/year used here is an independent modest planning prior, not thatQALY divided/repeated. No separatefall benefit added.

evidence.result: Two-year pain/function outcomes not significantly improved;23%watchfulwaiting crossed torepair.
evidence.transfer: Minimallysymptomatic benefit can be zero. .04utilityprior applies only to assumedselectedpain-limitingcases, not all201generalservices or a measuredsymptomaticsubgroup.

evidence.design: Observational positive-FIT cohort and methodological critique
evidence.transfer: Selection, nonprogramcare and exposure/immortal-time concerns remain. The new small fatal-hazard difference/latency/duration are explicit hypotheses, not extracted causalparameters.

reservations: Wholegift allocation is prospective, not auditedspecialtyspending. Mostserviceshaveunquantifiedhealth.
Alternativecare and provider-financing additionality dominate. No never-care assumption.
CRC mean-hazard model is not an exact mixture over individual random later-care times, nor a validated stage/adenoma simulation.
Cataract and symptomatic-hernia utilities are transferablepriorjudgments, not observedOA effects.
The CRC component is slightly negative centrally after conservative acuteprocedure harm. It was not forcedpositive.
Gross-associated resource cost is neither net induced nor exhaustive. Donatedcharges are not economicresources.
excludedBenefits: All remainingGI/general/eye and other-specialty health leftunquantified, withallcostsretained.
No extra cancer morbidity, adenoma prevention, second-eye benefit, fall prevention, productivity, familyQALY or lifetime credit.
No observed96%reportedhealthimprovement→QALY conversion, no94%readiness→completioneffect, and no donateddollar→healthconversion.
No publicreimbursement subtraction, donatedretailvaluation, netpayersavings or speculativeindirectlocalbenefit.
